instances.h: A published case, read as precedent

block.caption: Industry precedent, not our project record
block.h: A published case, read as precedent
block.intro: In July/August 2006, Pharmaceutical Engineering described a polypropylene Purified Water loop at a pilot plant. Two of its four authors worked for a water system maker. It is someone else's system, not proof of ours.

rows.v: Anything about our package
rows.m: Its sanitizing chemical, USP edition and design are its own, not a description of ours.

rows.v: Small solid-dose pilot plant
rows.m: Clinical supplies; water for the product, equipment and washing

rows.v: Polypropylene loop over stainless steel
rows.m: Also chosen over PVDF, on cost

rows.v: No routine heat sanitization
rows.m: The authors judged a simple PW loop does not need it, so plastic was acceptable

rows.v: Six weeks of performance qualification
rows.m: Samples from every point of use, three days a week. Today, WHO TRS 1033 sets three phases over 12 months.

rows.v: Over a year of weekly release testing
rows.m: Each excursion was investigated and closed, with a cause or follow-up tests
